title: Flowise chatflow delete -- T1485 either delete permission deletes either flow type, RBAC domains are not bound to resource type
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69262 (GHSA-p5w8-m249-4r4v),
affecting `DELETE /api/v1/chatflows/:id`.

The route authorizes with `checkAnyPermission('chatflows:delete,agentflows:delete')`
-- possession of EITHER permission is sufficient to reach the delete
path. The delete logic resolves the target record by `id` and
`workspaceId` and deletes it, with no check that the resolved
resource's actual type (`CHATFLOW` vs. `AGENTFLOW`) matches the
permission domain the caller was granted. An API key scoped to only
`agentflows:delete` can therefore delete a `CHATFLOW`, and a key
scoped to only `chatflows:delete` can delete an `AGENTFLOW` -- the
intended RBAC separation between the two resource types does not
actually bind to the type being acted on.

Detection logic flags a `DELETE /api/v1/chatflows/:id` request
authenticated with an API key or role whose granted permissions do
not include `chatflows:delete` -- the exact
permission-domain-crosses-resource-type gap this advisory's
reproduction confirms with a 200 OK deletion using an
`agentflows:delete`-only key.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact permission check, the missing type-binding
logic, and a step-by-step reproduction with the actual API key
permission set and observed 200 OK response), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
